title: Exploring Steady Beat with Percussion
description: Find and perform a steady beat through body percussion and classroom instruments.
fullDescription: Students connect a musical pulse to the heartbeat, practice it with body percussion, then transfer the beat to small percussion instruments.
materials: Small hand percussion, an audio recording, crayons, and the source worksheet.
teacherNote: Begin with clapping, patting, or stomping so every student can join before instruments are distributed.

title: Exploring Long and Short Rhythmic Patterns
description: Represent long and short sounds with movement, then compose in non-traditional notation.
fullDescription: Students hear and embody contrasting sound lengths, develop symbols for them, and organize those symbols into patterns they can perform.
materials: Open movement space, drawing materials, and the source activity sheet if desired.
teacherNote: Invite students to explain their symbols before the class performs each pattern.

title: Call and Response Songs
description: Practice musical turn-taking by listening, echoing, and leading short sung ideas.
fullDescription: A singing-centered introduction to call and response form that builds attentive listening and confidence entering at the right moment.
materials: Voices and a familiar call-and-response song selected by the teacher.
teacherNote: Use neutral syllables first, then let students invent calls that fit the class response.

title: Moving Melodies
description: Sing and show melodic direction with whole-body movement and visual contours.
fullDescription: Students trace the shape of a melody as it rises, falls, or repeats, making pitch relationships visible and physical.
materials: Open movement space, voices, and optional scarves or ribbon wands.
teacherNote: Mirror students' gestures and describe direction without requiring note names.

title: Performing and Composing Four-Beat Patterns
description: Read, perform, and create compact four-beat rhythms as a class and in small groups.
fullDescription: Students move from echoing four-beat patterns to reading and composing their own, reinforcing the relationship between symbols and sound.
materials: Board or chart paper, rhythm cards, and optional unpitched percussion.
teacherNote: Keep a visible four-beat frame on the board so students can check that each measure is complete.

title: Seat on the Beat
description: Perform and invent rhythmic patterns using the body as an instrument.
fullDescription: This active lesson develops pulse and pattern awareness through claps, pats, snaps, and other accessible body percussion sounds.
materials: Chairs or floor spots and enough room for safe seated movement.
teacherNote: Offer a quiet alternative gesture for students who are sensitive to loud claps or stomps.

title: Dynamics Hide and Seek
description: Use vocal dynamics as musical clues in a familiar hot-and-cold search game.
fullDescription: Students control and interpret changes in loudness while guiding a classmate toward a hidden object.
materials: A small object to hide and a safe, clearly bounded search area.
teacherNote: Set a comfortable maximum volume and practice a silent stop signal before the game begins.

title: Composing in Common Time
description: Compose and perform short rhythms in 4/4, 3/4, or 6/8 meter.
fullDescription: After reviewing steady beat and echo patterns, students create measures in simple or compound meter and teach them to classmates.
materials: The source student worksheet, pencils, and optional body percussion or instruments.
teacherNote: Choose one meter for a short lesson; compare meters only after students are secure in the first.

title: Classroom Thunderstorm
description: Create a one-minute storm using changes in dynamics, tempo, and articulation.
fullDescription: The class turns a familiar weather event into a conducted composition with crescendo, decrescendo, accelerando, ritardando, and accents.
materials: Bodies, optional non-pitched percussion, and a board or chart paper.
teacherNote: Repeat the piece with a student conductor once the class understands the musical vocabulary.

title: I've Got a Friend in Chicago
description: Listen to, analyze, and preserve music made by and for children in the United States.
fullDescription: Students explore children's musical culture through recordings, songs, chants, and games, then document music from their own community.
materials: The downloadable lesson plan, source recordings, and a simple way to record student work.
teacherNote: Treat students as culture-bearers: invite them to share playground music without ranking one version as the correct one.

title: Little Sir Orca
description: Use music, photographs, and inquiry to explore how humans and orcas make sound.
fullDescription: An arts-integrated entry point to careful listening and the animal world, adaptable across elementary grade levels.
materials: The Smithsonian lesson PDF, linked recordings, photographs, and classroom art materials.
teacherNote: Preview linked media and select the amount of science context that fits your grade band.

title: The Language of Rhythm
description: Turn spoken language into rhythms, then layer and perform them with body percussion.
fullDescription: Students connect natural speech rhythms to musical notation and performance, building material from words they already know.
materials: Board or chart paper and optional unpitched percussion.
teacherNote: Ask groups to speak their phrase clearly before transferring it to percussion sounds.

title: Musical Mapping
description: Use singing and movement to make first and second endings visible.
fullDescription: Students map musical routes through repeated sections, experiencing how alternate endings change the path through a piece.
materials: Open movement space, a familiar song with alternate endings, and optional floor markers.
teacherNote: Build the route physically before introducing notation symbols for repeat signs and endings.

title: Composing a Name Melody
description: Assign rhythm and pitch to the syllables of a name, then combine ideas into a group piece.
fullDescription: Students compose a one- or two-measure melody from a name, notate it, and collaborate on a longer class composition.
materials: The source teacher and student worksheets, pencils, and pitched classroom instruments if available.
teacherNote: Offer a limited pitch set for emerging composers and a wider range for students ready for more choice.

title: Yes! I Wanna! Music from Botswana
description: Sing, listen critically, and create a game and composition inspired by music from Botswana.
fullDescription: A three-lesson sequence that centers traditional instruments, vocal style, critical listening, singing, and student creation.
materials: The downloadable Folkways lesson plan, linked recordings, and classroom percussion.
teacherNote: Use the source's cultural notes and recordings together; avoid presenting a single piece as representative of an entire country.

title: West African Songs & Chants
description: Explore children's music from Ghana through singing, chanting, dancing, and ensemble playing.
fullDescription: Students build experience with basic polyrhythmic ensembles while connecting musical actions to their cultural source.
materials: The downloadable lesson plan, source audio, and classroom percussion or body percussion.
teacherNote: Teach one layer at a time and keep the source recordings central to the learning process.

title: Ganggangsullae: Korean Dance Music
description: Study call-and-response and a regional melodic mode through Korean circle dance music.
fullDescription: Students listen, move, and learn about Ganggangsullae while developing vocabulary for musical form and melodic character.
materials: The Folkways lesson plan, source recordings, and an open, accessible movement space.
teacherNote: Preview movement adaptations so students can participate seated, standing, or with a partner as needed.

title: American Folk Song Primary-Source Lessons
source: Kodály Center at the University of Redlands
description: Connect folk songs to recordings, photographs, maps, field notes, and historical context.
fullDescription: A collection of cross-curricular lessons built around American Folklife Center material, with many songs suitable for classroom listening or singing.
materials: The selected lesson PDF and its linked Library of Congress primary sources.
teacherNote: Read the historical and cultural notes before choosing a song, and follow the collection's attribution guidance.

title: Musical Explorers Digital
description: Meet artists and musical traditions through free lessons, recordings, videos, and concert experiences.
fullDescription: Each program includes artist-centered units with songs, musical concepts, cultural context, creative extensions, and multiple pathways for classroom use.
materials: The selected digital program's teacher guide, audio, videos, and optional extension materials.
teacherNote: Choose the Explore, Enhance, or Discover pathway based on available class time and student needs.
